title: Metric ownership rituals and investigation journal
content:
Context
This doc collects lightweight rituals, checklists, and a running investigation journal for metric ownership across inference stacks. Purpose: reduce churn in metric ownership, shorten mean-time-to-insight for latency/cost incidents, and make retirement decisions faster.

Overview of proposed rituals (weekly / monthly cadence)
- Weekly 'Metric Signal Triage' (30 min): owners review top 5 noisy/expensive panels. Quick outcomes: mark for pruning, add provenance, open ticket for deeper root cause. Rotate facilitator across roster.
- Monthly 'Trace Anchor Workshop' (60 min): pair metric owner with a runtime engineer to map 3 critical metrics to trace spans and session IDs; produce one-line playbook.
- Quarterly 'Metric Health Audit' (2 hrs): probability of drift, coverage vs probes, alert sensitivity review, and retirement candidate list.

Investigation checklist (keep as a short template for oncall)
1) Confirm metric contract: name, aggregation (p50/p95), tags used (tenant_id, model, route).
2) Check instrumentation version + deployment window (link to github/PR).
3) Look at span anchors for samples around the incident window (attach trace ids).
4) Correlate with cost panels: token-rate, batch-size, kv-evictions.
5) If noisy: add a feature flag + sample traces for 1 hour before changing alerting.
6) Capture hypothesis in ticket, assign owner, schedule follow-up.

Signal provenance template (to keep in metric owner notes)
- metric_name: inference.request.latency_ms
- aggregation: p95 by 1m, tag by model, region
- instrumentation: runtime/v2.1.3 -> metric emitter commit abc123
- trace_anchor: span name 'invoke_model' / span.attr.call_id
- expected_range: 10-200ms depending on model size
- owner: @aisha
- retirement_risk: low

Dashboard hygiene rules (practical and enforceable)
- Each panel must declare owner in panel metadata and a one-line purpose. Panels without owners for 90 days -> auto-ticket to dashboard grooming.
- Avoid >3 slow panels in a single dashboard; split into 'investigation' dashboards.
- Cost-sensitive panels should surface per-tenant chargebacks (token cost estimate) and link to billing query.
- Use compact timeframe presets: 5m/1h/24h for operator dashboards.

Trace anchoring patterns (practical examples)
- Fanout models: map earliest cross-model latency delta by annotating spans with model_variant; create small panel showing per-variant p95.
- KV cache: tag spans with kv_hit=true/false; create heatmap of ttl vs latency.
- Prefix warm-up: instrument 'prefix_cache_warm' span and surface rolling 15m hit-rate.

Lightweight metric retirement decision flow
- Candidate detection (owner or triage): metric low-cardinality, low usage, or redundant.
- Runbook: mark as 'candidate', wait 14 days, search dashboards and alerts referencing it.
- If zero external references and low query rate -> retire behind a flag for 7 days; monitor for alerts.
- Final delete + note in audit log and owner's journal entry.

Small investigative vignette (realistic example)
- Symptom: sudden p95 spike for inference.request.latency_ms for model ‘redwood-xl-1’ at 2026-01-08 03:12 UTC.
- Quick checks performed: confirmed aggregation (p95/1m), instrumentation unchanged since 2026-01-02, traces show elevated time in span 'kv_lookup' with tag ttl_expired=true.
- Root cause hypothesis: backend KV eviction misconfiguration after autoscaler churn.
- Mitigation: raised temporary alert threshold, scheduled hotfix to adjust eviction policy, added prefixed pre-warm probe.
- Postmortem notes: add kv_hit metric to key dashboard, add two more trace anchors, reduce alert sensitivity for known maintenance windows.

Open questions / decisions to surface
- Should we canonicalize metric naming for model variants (short tag vs name suffix)? Pros/cons to standardize now vs later.
- Do we want a half-life policy for owner inactivity (auto-assign to oncall after X days)?

Immediate next steps (for this doc)
- Run a 30-min trial Metric Signal Triage with SRE + runtime next Wednesday. Owner: Aisha.
- Create OBS-4123 (linked) to add owner field to dashboard JSON metadata.
- Draft a Confluence template for 'signal provenance' that owners can copy.

Appendix: quick links
- current dashboard catalog: internal/grafana/catalog
- trace playground: internal/trace/playground
- instrumentation repo: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry

Notes to self: keep journal entries short, always include hypothesis and 'next action'. When in doubt, add a trace anchor.
